correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs all quantifiers and constants. The focal infinite-kernel formula for \(d_+\) is used exactly; the Hilbert orthogonal projection has norm \(1\); the inverse and Neumann-series bounds are explicit; and the derivative of \(B_\varepsilon(s)\) has positive numerator \(\varepsilon(1-s)^2+s^2\). The two displayed restrictions on \(\varepsilon\) prove the two required strict inequalities. No finite experiment is promoted to an infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The focal paper introduces \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{SF}}\), records only the factor-two weaker Hilbertian lower bound, and asks for quantitative comparison with uniform subprojectivity. The new result identifies the best possible universal coefficient of this natural obstruction profile. Hilbert space proves coefficient \(1\) is sharp, so the improvement is structural rather than an arbitrary numerical tuning.
